correctness.rationale: At 1<=t<=2 the axial facet is a diamond of area 2(t-1)^2 and the diagonal facet is an octant triangle with three disjoint corners removed; for 2<=t<=3 axial facet area loses four right triangles, and the diagonal facet is a cut-corner triangle with area sqrt(3)(3-t)^2/2. Removing six disjoint caps from the octahedron or eight tetrahedra from the cube gives the two V(t) formulas. Cauchy's area formula pairs antipodal facets, giving the three axial and four diagonal symmetric generators with the specified coefficients and no residual factor of two. I enumerated determinant magnitudes using the alternate diagonal representatives (1,±1,±1); the independent sum is 8a^3+96a²b+192ab²+128b³. The replay python /workspace/reproduce_frozen.py independently factors both derivatives and gives their common t=2 value 108/125. The two displayed bijective rational substitutions give one coefficient sign change each, with opposite signs at the interval endpoints; this proves exactly one critical point in each interval. The denominators have opposite signs before cubing, producing the asserted decrease/increase/decrease. As an independent upper-bound check on [2,3], set s=3-t. The profile is (8-3s^4+3s^6/4)/(1-s³/6)^2; subtract its numerator from nine times the denominator to obtain 1-3s³(1-s)-s^6/2, at least 47/256 on [0,1] since s³(1-s)<=27/256. Hence the value 9 is unique at 1. Monotonicity, P(3/2)=127/16<8, P(2)=207/25>8 and P(3)=8 give the unique global minimum and both level-eight crossings, including no additional crossings strictly after t=2. The diagonal facet vertices for 1<t<2 are the permutations of (1,t-1,0); their centroid is (t/3,t/3,t/3) and central symmetry forces t=3/2, so the strict interval contains nonzonotopes. The independent replay confirms all displayed critical/crossing approximations; root counts are analytical, not inferred by numerical sampling. Frozen checker inspected, not run.
